title: Louis Armstrong's role on her records and rehearsals
summary: She says Louis followed her on the records, played only between songs, and did not need to rehearse every day.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: When you played with Louie Armstrong, he followed you -- you were the more important one, weren't you, on those early records?
And he just followed along with you?

I think so. (Unintelligible) -- see, I didn't live in Chicago, but I stayed there most of the time I was recording and you see, records I recorded. But everytime I'd go, I'd stay there six months at a time, six months out of each year, sometime nine months. Sometime I stay six months and then skip three and play six more months, you know, something like that. But everytime I'd stay, they would Louis to play. Louis just played

the trumpet. All I had to do was rehearse with my piano. Louis (unintelligible) played just like him and ________ might have been a little bit older than Herschel and his name was Andrew ________, something like that. And I used to go to his house to rehearse, you know, and Louis wouldn't have to be at rehearsal, because all he played was the trumpet. He only played in between the songs. After we sang them, you know, he just came in with his music between the song, you know. But (unintelligible) all the time. He didn't have to come to rehearse with us everyday like me and Andrew did, you know.
Did he ever rehearse at all with you or not at all? Did he just come and play?

He had to rehearse ________ an hour before ________. He had to do that, to see how a record -- to see how the timing's doing and see how it's going to go off in this room, then go in that room, and then ________.
That's when you were making it in the horn?
